newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan firm calls for joint oil exploration in disputed isles.
newsitem.headline: Japan firm calls for joint oil exploration in disputed isles.

text.p: A senior official at state-run Japan National Oil Corp (JNOC) called on Wednesday for the joint exploration of the East China Sea islands that have triggered a heated ownership dispute between China, Japan and Taiwan.
Akira Sakurai, vice president and a member of the JNOC board, said the disputed islands -- known as the Diaoyus to the Chinese and Senkakus to the Japanese -- potentially held oil and gas.

"Technically, the area has very good potential...as an oil man, I would like to start exploration as early as possible," he told Reuters on the sidelines of the annual Offshore Southeast Asia Conference.
A makeshift lighthouse built by a rightist Japanese group on one of the islands in July has rekindled a festering dispute over the islands, claimed by Tokyo, Beijing and Taipei.
Sakurai said a joint exploration of the islands could help ease the tension, citing similar territorial disputes between Japan and Korea, Thailand and Malaysia, Indonesia and Australia.
"Exploration activites afterward in these joint development areas have been producing good results," he said
Japan was given control of the islands in 1972 by the United States, which had administered them along with Okinawa since the end of World War Two.
Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
The islands are considered potentially rich in resources, including oil and gas as well as fish.
Japan and Taiwan must import almost all of their oil needs, and China's imports are rising rapidly as economic growth outpaces stagnant domestic production.
However, Japanese and Chinese oil sources said no exploration wells have yet been drilled in the area.
